observed_structure: One CUDA thread owns one output-frame and channel element after a flat-index guard against output_frames multiplied by channels.
The thread decomposes its flat index into channel and output frame, initializes one source-level FP32 accumulator to positive zero, and traverses taps in increasing integer order.
Each tap loads one BF16 input at output_frame multiplied by stride plus tap, converts it to FP32, and adds it to the accumulator.
After the tap loop, the kernel divides the FP32 sum by the runtime kernel extent and performs one BF16 conversion for the output store.
variant_notes: The collected Qwen2.5-Omni occurrence pins kernel two, stride two and floor-divided output length through its wider source path, while this cited kernel span itself accepts runtime kernel, stride and output-frame arguments.
The span contains no per-tap bounds branch and does not independently establish that host-provided output_frames makes every window in bounds, including the odd-frame tail case.
Source-level tap order, conversions and division do not establish generated instruction order, bitwise numerical equivalence, correctness, memory safety or performance.
This is one implementation ID in one Git blob, so it remains below the local two-implementation and two-blob candidate threshold.
